questions.q: What two variables primarily size the reusable network module built in this lesson?
options: subnet_ids and vnet_id
resource_group_name and vnet_id
environment and location only
vnet_address_space and subnet_count
questions.explain: The address space and the subnet count are the two real inputs that let the same module produce a differently sized network each time it's called.

questions.q: What does cidrsubnet() do inside the azurerm_subnet resource's address_prefixes argument?
options: Computes each subnet's CIDR block automatically from the parent address space, subnet_newbits, and count.index
Looks up a subnet's ID from Azure after it's created
Only works with AWS VPCs, not Azure VNets
Deletes a subnet that already exists
questions.explain: cidrsubnet() takes the parent block, how many bits to borrow, and an index, and returns a correct, non-overlapping subnet CIDR each time.

questions.q: Why doesn't modules/network itself contain a backend block?
options: Because backend configuration belongs to the calling root configuration, never to a child module
Because backend blocks are only allowed in Bicep, not Terraform
Because the module hasn't been published to the Terraform Registry yet
Because Azure doesn't support remote backends for virtual networks
questions.explain: A child module is never allowed to declare its own backend -- that's a property of the root configuration you actually run terraform init in.

questions.q: What three values does the network module's outputs.tf return?
options: The Azure subscription ID and tenant ID
environment, location, and subnet_newbits
vnet_id, subnet_ids, and resource_group_name
Only a single combined JSON blob
questions.explain: Those three outputs are exactly what a caller needs to wire other resources into this network without reaching into the module's internals.

questions.q: Why is subnet_ids built as azurerm_subnet.this[*].id rather than a single plain ID?
options: Because only the first subnet actually gets created
Because [*] converts a string into a number
Because subnet_count created multiple subnet resources via count, so the output must gather a list with the splat operator
Because Terraform requires every output to be a list regardless of context
questions.explain: count produces a list of resource instances, and [*] gathers one attribute from every instance in that list.
